title: Adjectives vs adverbs
keyIdea: An adjective describes a noun: the slow dog, the dog is slow. An adverb describes a verb, saying how an action is done: the dog walks slowly. Many adverbs are an adjective plus ly (quick, quickly), with spelling changes: y becomes i (happy, happily) and le becomes ly (gentle, gently). To choose, ask what the word tells about. After a doing word, use the adverb; after is, was or seems, the word still describes the noun, so use the adjective. Judge the job, not the ending: friendly is an adjective, and fast, hard and well are adverbs without ly.
familyTip: Play 'How did it go?' at home. One person does an action, like walking to the door. The other gives an adjective, like slow, and the walker has to change it into the adverb and act it out: slowly! Swap with happy (happily), gentle (gently) and noisy (noisily). Then catch each other's slips in chat, like 'You ate quick!', and fix them together.

visual.caption: Does the coloured word tell about a thing or about how it is done? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: link describing words to what they describe, bolt on the right ly ending, fill gaps, fix slips, sort by job not ending.

kid: Some words tell us more about other words. The slow dog. Slow tells us what the dog is like. Dog is a noun, a thing. A word that tells about a noun is an adjective.
Now read: the dog walks slowly. Slowly tells us how it walks. Walks is a verb, a doing word. A word that tells how a verb is done is an adverb.
Lots of adverbs are an adjective with ly on the end. Quick turns into quickly. If the word ends in y, the y turns into i: happy, happily. If it ends in le, the le turns into ly: gentle, gently.

To pick the right one, ask: is it about a thing, or about how it is done? The cat is quiet. Is is not an action, so we use quiet. Sam ran quickly. Ran is an action, so we use quickly. Watch out! Some words that end in ly are not adverbs, like a friendly cat. And fast, hard and well are adverbs with no ly: he ran fast, she swims well.
adult: Ages 7 to 8. The National Curriculum in England (Year 2 grammar) asks children to use adjectives in noun phrases and to add the suffix -ly to turn adjectives into adverbs; English Appendix 1 (Years 3 and 4) sets out the -ly spelling rules. CCSS L.2.1e asks second graders to use adjectives and adverbs and to choose between them depending on what is to be modified. Key terms: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, suffix, root word.

The test is the job the word does, not its shape. An adjective modifies a noun, either before it (the quiet cat) or after a linking verb such as be, seem, look or feel (the cat is quiet). An adverb modifies a verb, telling how, when or where the action happens (she sang sweetly). Spelling of -ly: most words just add it (soft, softly); a consonant then y changes y to i (easy, easily); a final le becomes ly (gentle, gently).

Common mistakes: using the adjective after an action verb (she ran quick, walk careful); adding ly after a linking verb because it sounds grand (the sun was brightly); spelling slips such as happyly and gentlely; deciding by the ending alone, so friendly, lovely and silly are called adverbs even though they describe nouns; and missing adverbs with no ly, such as fast, hard and well (good is the adjective, well the adverb: she plays well). Be careful with words that do both jobs, like fast in a fast car and he ran fast.

In the lab your child taps the word a describing word points at and sees an arrow to the noun or verb, drags +ly, y to ily or le to ly onto five adjectives, drags quick or quickly into sentence gaps, finds the wrong describing word in four sentences, and sorts eight cards by job, including friendly, fast and well. Every wrong move gets a reason that names the job of the word.

practice.prompt: Which word is right? The rabbit hopped ___.
practice.hint: Hopped is a doing word. Which word tells how it hopped?
practice.explain: quickly is the adverb. It tells how the rabbit hopped.

practice.prompt: Ben writes {n} adjectives. He adds ly to each one to make an adverb. How many adverbs does he make?
practice.hint: Each adjective with ly on the end makes one adverb.
practice.explain: One adverb from each adjective, so {n} adjectives make {n} adverbs.

practice.prompt: How do you spell gentle as an adverb?
practice.hint: The word ends in le. What happens to le?
practice.explain: gentle ends in le, so the le turns into ly: gently.

practice.prompt: A list has {a} adjectives and {b} adverbs. How many describing words is that in all?
practice.hint: Adjectives and adverbs are both describing words. Add them.
practice.explain: {a} adjectives and {b} adverbs make {=a+b} describing words.

practice.prompt: Which word is right? The soup is ___.
practice.hint: Is is not an action. Does the word tell about the soup?
practice.explain: hot tells about the soup, a thing, so it is the adjective. Is links it back to soup.

pool.prompt: In 'a lovely day', what kind of word is lovely?
pool.hint: Does lovely tell about a thing or about how something is done?
pool.explain: lovely tells about the day, a thing, so it is an adjective, even with ly at the end.

pool.hint: Spoke is a doing word. Check the spelling too.
pool.explain: politely tells how she spoke, so use the adverb. polite just adds ly.

pool.prompt: How do you spell noisy as an adverb?
pool.hint: noisy ends in y. What happens to the y?
pool.explain: The y changes to i, then add ly: noisily.

pool.prompt: In 'He ran fast', what does fast tell about?
pool.hint: Look at the doing word next to it.
pool.explain: fast tells how he ran, so here it is an adverb with no ly.

pool.prompt: Zoe finds {n} adverbs in a story. Each one tells how a verb is done. How many verbs do they describe?
pool.hint: Each adverb in the story goes with one verb.
pool.explain: Each adverb tells about one verb, so {n} adverbs describe {n} verbs.

pool.prompt: Which word is right? Dad sings ___.
pool.hint: The word tells how Dad sings. good is for things.
pool.explain: well is the adverb that goes with good. Dad sings well; it is a good song.

pool.prompt: Ali has {n} cards with adjectives. Each card can turn into an adverb with ly. He uses {k} of them. How many cards are left?
pool.hint: Take the cards he used away from the cards he had.
pool.explain: {n} cards take away {k} used leaves {=n-k} cards.

pool.hint: Was is not an action. What should tell about the sky?
pool.explain: After was, the word tells about the sky, so use the adjective bright. Shone brightly is right.

pool.prompt: In 'The tall girl ran quickly', which word is the adjective?
pool.hint: Find the word that tells about the girl.
pool.explain: tall tells about the girl, a noun. quickly is the adverb that tells how she ran.
